{{Quote|Our Emperor has called upon all of his loyal sectors to aid him in cutting off the trafficking in illegal weaponry. I am proud to say that I am responding to the Emperor's call in the most immediate and visceral terms. We all know that the source of much of the illegal gunrunning and drug trafficking emanates from Hutt space. To this end, I am calling on all citizens of our sector to support me as I shut down the Hutt scourge! It is my intention to wipe out the smuggling trade, and bring the Hutt crime lords to their knees! Um&hellip; figuratively speaking, of course.|[[Sarn Shild]]|<ref name="THG" />}}
'''Hutt Space''', also known as the '''Hutt sector''',<ref name="TPS">''[[The Paradise Snare]]''</ref> was an autonomous region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] on the border between the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] and the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], near the entrance to [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]]. It encompassed the [[Si'Klaata Cluster/Legends|Si'Klaata Cluster]], and bordered on the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]]. Hutt Space was named for the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] species, who dominated the region. Differing accounts attributed different numbers of planets in Hutt Space, but reasonable estimates ranged from a few hundred to a thousand inhabited worlds.

==History==
===Early Beginnings===
{{Quote|When Xim the Despot and his droid legions attempted to invade Hutt space, the great Kossak defeated them at Vontor and sent them fleeing for the Tion Hegemony.|[[Borga Besadii Diori]]|<ref name="JE">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref>}}
During the [[Pre-Republic era]], the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] originated on the world of [[Varl/Legends|Varl]]. It is unknown whether the Hutts developed interstellar technology or acquired it from another species due to conflicting historical accounts. An aggressive and expansionist warrior species, the Hutts invaded several outlying worlds and enslaved hundreds of other species; sometimes slavery was so heavy, and many slaves were sent to war to fight for the Hutts, that whole enslaved species perished.<ref name="TEA" /> Hutt Space was formed into the [[Hutt Empire]] sometime after [[25,200 BBY]] and for approximately the next two centuries, they were the most powerful government in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

In [[25,102 BBY]], the Hutts were challenged by the [[Human/Legends|Human]]/[[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] warlord [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] who had carved up a substantial interstellar [[Xim's empire|empire]] in the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. The Hutts had assembled a sizable mercenary army of [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]], [[Vodran (species)/Legends|Vodran]] and [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]] warriors, whose leaders ratified the [[Treaty of Vontor]] which bound the three species to a permanent state of servitude. Following a devastating war of two ritualistic battles, Xim's forces were routed by [[Kossak Inijic Ar'durv|Kossak the Hutt]] at the [[Third Battle of Vontor]] in [[25,096 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> With Xim eliminated, the Hutts then invaded and devastated much of the Tion Cluster. The Tionese were so debilitated militarily and economically that they did not pose a military threat for a long time. Meanwhile, the Hutts had ceased to be identified as an Empire within a century of Xim's defeat.<ref name="TEA" />

In [[24,000 BBY]], Hutt Space and the Tion Cluster were first encountered by the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]&mdash;based [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] which had discovered the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]]. Conflict between the Republic and the [[Honorable Union of Desevro and Tion|Honorable Union of Desevro & Tion]] led to the [[Tionese War]] which ended in the former's favor when Republic agents stirred up trouble in Hutt Space. The Hutts then (who were also worrying that the victor of the "ritual wars" would eventually unify both human "[[clan]]s") invaded the Tion Cluster and exterminated many of the Tionese within 12,000 [[Light-year/Legends|light-years]].<ref name="TNEC" /><ref name="TEA" /> The surviving Tionese appealed to their former Republic foes for protection and most of the Tionese worlds subsequently joined the Republic. With their human foes united, the Hutts prepared for a war against the human species and their supreme authority; until they realized that the humans were not a clan-based society, but a bureaucratic entity that included several species.<ref name="TEA" />
===The kajidic===
Around [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]], clan rivalries became so intense that resulted to destructive civil wars. Much of Hutt Space was devastated during these [[Hutt Cataclysms]]. The war rendered the Hutt homeworld of Varl and other colony worlds barren and incapable of sustaining life. The surviving Hutt clans relocated their capital to [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Evocar]] which they renamed Nal Hutta, having displaced and exiled the native [[Evocii]] to its moon [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. [[Budhila Hestilic Amura]] established the [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Hutt Ruling Council]] to oversee the activities of the Hutt kajidics and to mitigate rivalries. He also developed the philosophy of [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidic]] which promoted fierce inter-clan rivalry and infiltration of institutions in favor of war and expansionism.<ref name="TEA" />

The era of the Cataclysms and the reformation was so pivotal in Hutt history, that all previous eras were half-forgotten, and myth was mingled to conflicting accounts.<ref name="TEA" />
===Republic Entanglements===
{{Quote|Support the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Lord Jabba. The Republic's become a disease, and the Jedi are keeping it in power for their own ends, so help the systems that are breaking away to end that dictatorship once and for all. Because it is a dictatorship. Planets do things the Republic's way, or not at all. Otherwise, why not just let them cede from the alliance?''"<br />"''Hutt worlds aren't part of the Republic. We're separate already.|[[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] and [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]|<ref name="TCWn">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:Clone_wars_factions.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Hutt Space and its surrounding sphere of influence at its peak (depicted in green).]]
In the following centuries, the Hutts and the Republic ratified treaties that established the boundaries between the Republic and Hutt Space. Spacers also discovered the [[Ootmian Pabol/Legends|''Ootmian Pabol'']] trade route that linked the Republic frontiers with Nal Hutta and Nar Shaddaa, added to the older Tionese routes that connected the Perlemian to [[Sleheyron/Legends|Sleheyron]]. Due to increasing trade with the Republic, Sleheyron and Nar Shadaa developed rapidly, and Nal Hutta came to rival [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] as a center of interstellar trade.<ref name="TEA" /> 

In [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000 BBY]], the Republic came under the influence of the theocratic and [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] [[Pius Dea]] sect which posited [[Contispex I/Legends|Contispex I]] as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]].<ref name="TNEC" /> Taking advantage of the unpopularity of the Hutts among the Republic's citizens, Constipex sanctioned a [[Pius Dea Crusades|crusade]] against the Hutts. Over the following centuries, his descendants sanctioned several crusades against some rival alien sects in the Outer Rim which fought back; leaving the galaxy in a never-ending state of alternating hot and cold wars.<ref name="TTSP">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref> The anti-alien nature of the crusades precipitated an exodus into Hutt Space until the end of Pius Dea rule in [[11,000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> The repercussions of these crusades would sour relations between the Core and the outlying regions over the millennia.<ref name="TNEC" />

Nonetheless Hutt interests infiltrated not only the Republic underworld, but also the [[Megacorporation/Legends|megacorporations]] and institutions. [[Blotus]] was a significant Republic [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]].<ref name="TEA" />

However trade along the ''Ootmian'' was disrupted by a [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]] which destroyed the [[Kyyr system]] in [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]] and created the [[Thornhedge Nebula/Legends|Thornhedge Nebula]]. This coupled by the rise of the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]] ended Nal Hutta and Nar Shaddaa's existence as a legitimate trade center and it devolved over the millennia into a crime haven. The Hutts were not alarmed by the Republic expansion into the nearby [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] and [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], but rather infiltrated and took over the economies of these colonies, even to worlds well outside the Hutt Space.<ref name="TEA" />

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Hutt Space remained neutral amidst the fighting and played both Republic and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] against each other. However, in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], after [[Battle of Teth/Legends|rescuing]] and [[Mission to Jabba's Palace (Clone Wars)/Legends|returning]] [[Rotta/Legends|Rotta]] to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] at the neighboring [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis sector]], they allowed the Republic to pass through the sector unlike the CIS.<ref name="TEA" />

===[[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]]===
{{Quote|The Emperor has called upon all Imperial worlds to tighten down on smuggling, gunrunning, and other illegal activities. My sector contains Hutt space, and unfortunately the Hutt reputation for dishonesty is so well known that I cannot possibly cover for them. I will, however, promise Nal Hutta no armed reprisals if they cooperate.''"<br />"''Cooperate in what way?''"<br />"''Do their best to become loyal, law-abiding citizens of the Empire.|[[Sarn Shild]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="THG">''[[The Hutt Gambit]]''</ref>}}
During the rule of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the extent of the region had stabilized to a fixed size.

Portions of Hutt Space were reorganized into various sectors governed by the [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the [[Baxel sector/Legends|Baxel sector]], according to the Imperial treaty; however the [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] translation of the treaty did not mention a Moff, but a [[Consul/Legends|Consul]]. As a result, the Moff's authority (first Moff [[Sarn Shild]], and later Moff [[Yref Orgege]]) was weak at best and non-existent at worst.<ref name="TEA" />

The Hutts were occasionally expected (although they usually outmaneuvered) to show obeisance to the Emperor. The Empire relied to the Hutt Council to rule the countless Hutt crime lords and kajidics, and the Council arranged for considerable taxes to support the greatly expanded [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]]. As such, Hutt Space was left alone by the Empire, though the latter established some manufacturing facilities in parts of Hutt Space. Still, the Empire used its military as a bargaining chip in relations with Hutt Space, and occasionally moved against specific kajidics, or sent agents against Hutt operatives.<ref name="TEA" /> 

The Empire cracked down on slavery to some extent, but the Hutt Space, and several other entities, were immune from this ruling; when it started to hurt the trade, the Hutts quickly won several of the other interests and cooperatives. They also continued to focus on the Rimward territories, and bought-off the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] sectors that were nominally belonged and were organized by the Empire.<ref name="TEA" /> 

In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], [[Sriluur/Legends|Sriluur]] and its neighbors were annexed by the Empire while a token Imperial force unsuccessfully attempted to annihilate Nar Shaddaa shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Imperial forces also undertook police actions against individual kajidics that worked with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|fragmentation]] of the Empire, Hutt Space retained the same status quo during the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[New Republic era|period]], and remained mostly neutral throughout the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|fighting]] between Republic and the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]].<ref name="TEA" />

===[[Post-Imperial era/Legends|Post-Imperial era]]===
{{Quote|Executor Nom Anor has assured us that we will receive a warm reception in a nearby sector known as Hutt space, as the reigning species&mdash;the Hutts&mdash;have no wish to engage us in warfare.|[[Raff]], to [[Nas Choka]]|<ref name="HT">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos I: Hero's Trial]]''</ref>}}
During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]], much of Hutt Space was devastated in retribution for the Hutts' double-dealings with the Yuuzhan Vong and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. Several prominent Hutt worlds including Nal Hutta, Nar Shaddaa and [[Ilos]] were devastated or "[[Terraforming/Legends|Vongformed]]" by the invaders. The surviving Hutt kajidics were forced to relocate to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and Hutt territory was laid waste in the process. However, the worlds in the heart of Hutt Space known as ''[[Bootana Hutta/Legends|Bootana Hutta]]'' managed to resist the invaders since they were defended by Hutt warships, a rare sight in other regions. Additionally, the Hutt worlds mysteriously proved resistant to Yuuzhan Vong terraforming efforts. It was rumored among [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] and [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] alike that these secluded worlds were the source of a biotechnology which allowed the Hutts to resist "Vongforming".<ref name="TEA" />

With the Yuuzhan Vong's defeat in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]], the Hutts reasserted control over many of their worlds particularly Nal Hutta and Nar Shaddaa and sought to dominate regional reconstruction efforts, where the ''Bootana Hutta'' world of [[Mulatan]], became the third at last known capital of the oversector. In [[39 ABY]], Hutt Space refused to join the [[Five Worlds]] and remained independent from both the Five Worlds and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. However in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], when the [[Confederation]] was formed, Hutt Space joined the organization, and [[41 ABY|eventually]] the [[Hutt underground|Hutts]] themselves joined the members of the Oversector during the [[Second Galactic Civil War|great conflict]] with some kajidics, who only remained in the ''Bootana Hutta'', contributed warships.<ref name="TEA" />

By [[44 ABY]], the Klatooinians began to resent their status of eternal [[Slavery/Legends|servitude]] to the Hutts as decreed by the Treaty of Vontor in exchange for the Hutts protecting their sacred [[Fountain of Ancients|Fountain of the Ancients]] on their homeworld of [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]]. Tensions reached their climax when the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] led by [[Sarasu Taalon]] attacked the Fountain in an attempt to secure samples of [[wintrium]]. The Sith were quickly overpowered and sentenced to their death by the Klatooinians, whom then sought to liberate themselves from Hutt servitude by claiming that the Hutts violated the Treaty. Despite the mediation efforts of [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]], the Klatooinians began a full-scale uprising across Klatooine resulting in planet-wide skirmishes and firefights. The revolt rapidly gained galactic-wide attention particularly [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Natasi Daala|Daala]] who was concerned by the chaos caused by many anti-slavery uprisings across the galaxy.<ref name="Allies">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]''</ref>

By [[137 ABY]], a [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|New Galactic Empire]] under the control of the [[One Sith|Sith]] had usurped control of the Galaxy. For unknown reasons, Hutt Space provided covert help to the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]], one of the new Empire's major opponents. Later, the Sith's [[Devastation of Da Soocha|poisoning]] of [[Da Soocha]] and the destruction of the [[Hutt Temple]] [[Maya Armus]] on [[Napdu]] prompted the Hutts into entering the conflict against the Sith on the side of the Alliance and Imperials.<ref name="SWL48">[[Legacy (2006) 48|''Legacy'' (2006) 48]]</ref>

==Astrography==
Hutt Space changed sizies and shapes throughout the millennia. Although contact with the Galactic Republic stabilized its coreward borders through several treaties, the Hutts expanded their dubious operations rimward (with the Hutt Space as a "shield" from the Republc's eye) using the ''[[Shag Pabol/Legends|Shag Pabol]]'', which, as the name indicated, was used mainly for slavery. Rich clan throneworlds comprised the ''[[Pabol Hutta/Legends|Pabol Hutta]]'' which linked Sleheyron with Nal Hutta. The size and shape of the Space somehow stabilized around the time after the Clone Wars.<Ref name="TEA" />

External hyperlanes connected Hutt Space with the Tion Cluster, which brought conlfict within the two cultures, and later it was used for trade with the Republic. Upon Republic contact, the ''Ootmian Pabol'' connected Hutt Space with the Republic, contributing to Nar Shadaa's and Sleheyron's boom, until the cataclysm of the [[Kyyr system]].<Ref name="TEA" />

==Politics==
{{Quote|We are not far from Hutt space. Perhaps we could make contacts with other Hutt lords&hellip; see if they'd be willing to help.''"<br />"''Help? Hutts? They may contribute, and some have, but they do it for their own reasons, trust me, and those reasons have nothing to do with our aims. Hutts are devious&hellip; but sometimes their goals and ours coincide. That's when they hand out their credits. Half the time we can't even guess what benefit they may be getting as a result of their 'donation.'|[[Winfrid Dagore]] and [[Bria Tharen]]|<ref name="RD">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref>}}
Hutt Space was what remained of the ancient Hutt Empire, which existed in the times before [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]]. The [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Hutt Ruling Council]] controlled the region by overseeing the activities of the Hutt clans ([[Kajidic/Legends|kajidics]]) and their criminal syndicates. It was considered a lawless expanse within the Outer Rim Territories that was controlled by the most powerful and corrupt of Hutt clans. This meant it held an infamous reputation due to the widespread smuggling, piracy and open criminal activity.<ref name="TEGTW" />

The heart of the region contained the ''[[Bootana Hutta/Legends|Bootana Hutta]]'', the "Garden of the Hutts", an area containing the various Kajidic throneworlds. Even in the Empire's days, this area remained secretive to outsiders, who knew it only through rumors.<ref name="TEA" />

Relations with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] were typically strained, as this area served as a base for much of the criminal enterprise in the galaxy. The economic and strategic benefits of their relationship often encouraged both sides to compromise however, notably the Hutts sided with the Republic during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and were prevented from siding with them in the [[Great Galactic War]] only by the hard fought actions of [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]].

Their relationship with the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] were less cordial, with [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Naat Reath]] stating that Hutts had no love for Jedi. This was mostly due to the nature of a Jedi's work. The criminals they hunted would often flee into Hutt Space and the Hutts would be forced to deal with the imposition of a law enforcement official in their territory who they could neither bribe nor kill without consequence. However in practice the Jedi normally tried hard to avoid antagonizing the Hutts any more than they had to, standard operating procedure was to keep their presence very quiet or announce their presence to the local Hutt leader before proceeding. Though Hutts did not like Jedi messing with their affairs, some would find their presence an amusement or an opportunity, and many were eager to help them finish their business quickly and leave.
